issues.description: Mismatch in the data type of Person.id across artifacts. The problem statement's UML and the template repository define Person.id as a UUID, and the server-side services/controllers expect UUID (e.g. PersonService and PersonResource use UUID and UUID.randomUUID()). However, the solution repository's common Person class defines id as Long. This creates a compile-time/type incompatibility (e.g., PersonService in the solution calls person.setId(UUID.randomUUID()) while Person.setId expects a Long) and would confuse students about the intended id type and how to implement/consume the API.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the Person.id type across all artifacts. Prefer aligning with the problem statement and template (UUID): change the solution repository's common Person class to use UUID for id (private UUID id; with corresponding getter/setter). Ensure all usages (PersonService, PersonResource, client-side code) work with UUID. Alternatively, if Long was intentional, update the template and problem statement to state Long and change all server/client code to use Long consistently — but the least disruptive and clearer fix is to make the solution Person.id a UUID to match the template and specification.
